transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya with Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, i'll kick us off. we have Arjun from our SE team to walk through quickstart and benchmarks.
00:18 Priya Nair: thanks, maya. quick high level — we're exploring adding a small LLM feature to our product for assistant style q&a and search rerank. main concerns are latency under 200ms for short responses, and not exploding cost.
00:31 Ethan Cole: hi all, infra here. we also need to make sure whatever we pick can meet our data residency and audit requiremants, and SSO with our okta.
00:40 Arjun Patel: great, thanks. quick outline: we can get you to first token in under five minutes with Redwood hosted API via our PLG quickstart — free credits, sample curl, and an SDK. then for scale you can move to Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) if you need isolation and reserved capacity.
00:58 Marta Ruiz: how does the free credits work? is it one-off or per-team?
01:04 Maya Chen: typically we give an account credit to run the quickstart and a couple of sandbox projects. it's meant to let product and eng hit first token, run a couple of requests and smoke test. we'll send the instructions after this call.
01:20 Priya Nair: time-to-first-token, like actual token returned, not onboarding time?
01:25 Arjun Patel: yes — actual token. for hosted it's usually very quick: you sign up, we provision keys, you run curl with the sample prompt and you get streaming or non-streaming tokens. sometimes there is a 1-2 minute delay while we verify the account but usually sub-5 mins.
01:42 Ethan Cole: ok cool. on infra — if we wanted dedicated, is that a separate contract? what's the timeline?
01:49 Maya Chen: Dedicated is reserved capacity, it requires a commit and provisioning time — typically 2-4 weeks depending on region and GPU profile. for POC we recommend starting on hosted to validate, then we can map throughput needs to a Dedicated sizing.
02:04 Priya Nair: and private for on-prem / VPC?
02:07 Arjun Patel: Private is customer-managed — we ship a control plane or you run our package in your VPC/on-prem. there are options for KMS/HSM integrations for keys, audit logs export, and SOC2/ISO documentation. setup is longer, usually 6-12 weeks depending on network and compliance.
02:27 Marta Ruiz: do you support SAML/SSO?
02:30 Maya Chen: yes, SSO via SAML/OIDC is supported; for enterprise we offer SCIM for user provisioning and RBAC in the Console.
02:39 Ethan Cole: curious about KV cache and batching — how much of an impact on latency and cost?
02:44 Arjun Patel: good q. Redwood's runtime uses KV cache and prefix caching to avoid re-eval for repeated contexts; for many chat workloads that can reduce token compute by 20-60% and improve p99 latency. continuous batching is workload aware — you can trade a little latency for cost by batching.
03:02 Priya Nair: any quantization impacts? we saw models with int8 drop perf a bit on accuracy.
03:07 Arjun Patel: yes quantizashun (laugh) — quantization can affect quality. Redwood provides model profiles and recommendations — we surface perf/quality tradeoffs and suggest which quantization to use per workload.
03:20 Marta Ruiz: what about benchmarking — can you run one against our sample prompts and distrib?
03:24 Arjun Patel: absolutely, we can run a benchmark. easiest path is you share a small prompt set and we run hosted runs; if you need more realistic throughput we can run Dedicated test with a temporary seat.
03:36 Priya Nair: security paperwork — do you have SOC2 and data processing addendum?
03:40 Maya Chen: yes, SOC 2 Type II and DPA are available. we'll share security pack including pen test summary and network diagrams.
03:50 Ethan Cole: ok, also interested in KMS integration for customer-managed keys.
03:54 Arjun Patel: supported — KMS integrations and HSM for Private. for Hosted we also have envelope encryption options and audit logs.
04:05 Priya Nair: can you give rough pricing for hosted per token and for dedicated commit?
04:11 Maya Chen: i'll include pricing ranges in the follow up. hosted is usage-based (per-token/per-embedding). Dedicated is a reserved monthly commit that gives you predictable throughput; i'll put sample numbers for our typical gen and embedding workloads.
04:24 Marta Ruiz: any common objections you see when customers start with hosted?
04:28 Arjun Patel: main ones — data residency, compliance, and spike protections. we handle those with region pinning, private options, and routing policies. also cost surprises, which is why we recommend running our optimizer and cost profiling in the Console.
04:44 Priya Nair: competitors — we looked at OpenAI and anthropic; some teams like the hosted simplicity, others want more control. how do you position against those?
04:54 Maya Chen: we focus on production-first, unified experience across hosted/dedicated/private. so you get simple self-serve, then smooth path to dedicated or private with same API and rollout tools.
05:05 Ethan Cole: any gotchas in the quickstart for eng? we want minimal deps and sample code in our stack (node/python).
05:11 Arjun Patel: quickstart includes curl, python, and node examples, plus SDK snippets. it also has a small init script to pull model profiles and set up caching. should be 10-15 minutes to run locally and see tokens streaming.
05:25 Priya Nair: ok sweet. success criteria for a pilot — what should we aim for?
05:29 Maya Chen: agree on a few measurable things: latency targets (p50/p95), cost per 1k tokens, and quality metrics (eval prompt set pass rate). for PLG pilot we often set a 2-4 week sandbox where product owners validate UX and eng evaluates integration effort.
05:47 Marta Ruiz: for our team, we'd like p95 under 400ms for short answers and cost below x (we'll provide target).
05:53 Arjun Patel: noted. we'll run a sample benchmark and include p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens.
06:00 Ethan Cole: what about rate limits and quotas?
06:03 Maya Chen: hosted has rate limits per account; Console exposes token-level breakdowns and you can request higher quotas. dedicated gives predictable throughput and SLA.
06:13 Priya Nair: can you show the Console quickly?
06:15 Arjun Patel: yes i can demo next time — it has per-route dashboards, tracing hooks, and rollout controls — can do canary and A/B with automatic fallback. for today i'll keep it high level.
06:29 Maya Chen: quick recap and next steps in a sec. any other immediate q's?
06:32 Priya Nair: one more — we use snowflake for analytics and pinecone for vectors, any integrations?
06:38 Arjun Patel: we have export hooks and connectors; for embeddings we have common patterns with vector DBs like Pinecone, and you can export logs to S3 or stream to Snowflake via our exports.
06:52 Marta Ruiz: perfect.
06:54 Maya Chen: ok next steps: i'll send the quickstart guide, free credits instructions, security pack and pricing. Arjun will provision a benchmark run if you share the prompt set. priya will confirm stakeholders and residency. we'll also schedule the Console demo for next week.
07:12 Priya Nair: sounds good — i'll share prompts and security contact by friday.
07:16 Ethan Cole: i'll loop in infra SREs.
07:18 Marta Ruiz: i'll coordinate product acceptance criteria.
07:22 Maya Chen: great — thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the notes and links.
